articles.title: All-round boost for India ahead of Afghanistan T20Is; Jasprit Bumrah remains on track
articles.summary: Cricket News: India are set to get a major boost ahead of the T20I series against Afghanistan starting later this month. All-rounders Hardik Pandya and Nitish Kumar.
articles.body: India are set to get a major boost ahead of the T20I series against Afghanistan starting later this month. All-rounders Hardik Pandya and Nitish Kumar Reddy are on track as of now, while Washington Sundar is nearing the necessary clearances for the fixtures starting September 13 in Delhi. It is reliably learnt that Reddy has been training intensely at the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) and operating at full capacity in order to return to international cricket.As for Washington Sundar, he spent the weekend in Chennai and will report back to the CoE this week to prove his fitness before selection. The men's senior selection committee chaired by Ajit Agarkar is likely to meet this week to pick the squad for the three T20Is."The practical target is the T20Is against Afghanistan and this will allow Washington Sundar to ease back into the set-up with the shortest format. His workload has gradually increased in the last few weeks, and he could be available for selection for the three T20Is," says a source tracking developments."Both Reddy and Pandya have been at the CoE for a very long time now and only take breaks for personal commitments. Reddy only goes back home during the weekends while Pandya has anyway moved base to Bengaluru," adds the source.All eyes, however, are on Jasprit Bumrah. The fast bowler missed the two Tests against Sri Lanka earlier this month and the management wants to handle him very carefully with an eye on the two Tests against New Zealand later this year. The 32-year-old has been training at the CoE. While the Afghanistan T20Is could be touch-and-go, the Asian Games shouldn't face any availability issues if there are no late hiccups during his rehabilitation."Bumrah is progressing well. In buildup to the 2027 World Cup, the plan was that he would focus on ODIs and Tests but since the knee injury, the management wants to ease him back with the shortest format first. He is being closely monitored and while the Afghanistan T20Is could be too close for comfort, the Asian Games seem highly likely, provided there are no late surprises," explains the source.Krunal Pandya back in the mix?After the recent outings in Ireland and England, the Indian team management is exploring options of left-arm spinners in the shortest format. Axar Patel played all seven games and had mediocre returns: two wickets in four T20Is against England and two wickets in two T20Is against Ireland. Krunal Pandya is being discussed, and his return to the T20I squad would not be a surprise.Krunal, who last played for India in 2021 T20 series against Sri Lanka, has been very impressive in the IPL and picked up 14 wickets for the Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the 2026 edition. It now remains to be seen whether the selectors revert to a proven performer as they look to find the right candidate for the crucial left-arm spinner spot.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I felt sorry for the guy': Eight years later, Faf du Plessis revisits one of cricket’s darkest chapters; 'Sandpaper Gate', and believes Australia handled the scandal poorly
articles.summary: Cricket News: Eight years after the Sandpaper Gate scandal shook Australian cricket, former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has offered a different perspective .
articles.body: Eight years after the Sandpaper Gate scandal shook Australian cricket, former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has offered a different perspective on one of the most controversial episodes in the sport.Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper to alter the ball during the 2018 Cape Town Test against South Africa, setting off a scandal that engulfed the Australian team. Steve Smith and David Warner were also punished, with all three players losing their leadership positions or facing lengthy suspensions.But du Plessis believes Bancroft, in particular, was subjected to an unnecessarily harsh media trial. Speaking to former South Africa pacer Vernon Philander on the ‘Beyond the Boundary’ podcast, he said his immediate reaction was sympathy for the young Australian batter.“Bancroft, and honestly, my first instincts with him were, I felt sorry for the guy. When I saw him, first of all, he did that, and I was like, ‘Shame.’ He doesn't know what to do. He doesn't know how to get the ball to reverse swing, because taking a piece of sandpaper out of your pocket with cameras, it's not the most clever thing to do,” Faf said.The incident quickly escalated beyond the field. Du Plessis recalled how the South African team waited for Australia's press conference following the day's play, only to see the situation become even more explosive after the Australian team's statement.“Then it was that whole incident. I mean, we were sitting after the day's play. And we were like, the team is taking like an hour before the press conference has to start. So we're like, why are they taking so long? What are they doing? And then they issued that statement. And that statement was just like putting blitz under a fire and just going there. And they were saying, no one knows about it. The captain had no idea. The coach had no idea. And everyone was just like, well, hang on, what's going on here? Everyone knows what goes on in a dressing room,” he added.Du Plessis questions Australia’s responseThe scandal eventually saw Smith and Warner handed 12-month bans, while Bancroft was suspended for nine months. Smith and Warner were also removed from their leadership positions.Du Plessis believes Cricket Australia made the situation considerably bigger by allowing outside pressure, including political intervention, to influence its response.“So I think it was more the way that they handled that that caused a lot of noise. And then it went back to Australia, where the Australian Prime Minister got involved. The ex-cricketers were smashing the team about how you can do that? And we were sitting there going, come on, guys. It's not like you guys got a first to do it. You never did it. Like, don't be glasshouse,” said Faf.He also recalled reaching out to Smith during the fallout because he expected the punishment to last weeks or perhaps a month, rather than an entire year.“Everyone has done it at some stage in their career. Warner, Smith and Bancroft were the three guys who were actually caught. I felt the right thing to do was to send Steve Smith a message and say, Listen, I know you guys are trying to do the right thing. You're going to go through some crap over the next week. I thought it would be like a week or a month. But it ended up being a year. I was just like, I'm sorry you're going through this. You shouldn't take the brunt of this. It's a thing that, unfortunately, should fall on the whole team. But yeah, I felt for Bancroft. I felt sorry for him because he just didn't know how to do it. And Steve Smith for trying to do the right thing to be the captain and say, it's my show,” he added.Faf says bans were unnecessaryDu Plessis went further, arguing that the players should not have been removed from international cricket for such long periods.In his view, the International Cricket Council should have handled the disciplinary side of the incident, while Cricket Australia could have imposed financial penalties instead of lengthy bans.“I think they could have handled that a little bit better. Cricket Australia had other ideas. And they made that thing become a very big thing. Just let the ICC deal with it. I think when you let politics and stuff come into sport, it never ends well. And that's the case with the Prime Minister's politics and everyone putting pressure on them. And they're feeling like they have to act. They have to act to show that they're doing something. I think that becomes a dangerous precedent,” said Faf.Du Plessis suggested that the punishment could instead have been limited to match-fee deductions, allowing the players to continue their careers without missing an entire year.“I think if they took it on the chin on that night and said, Cameron would have said, I'm sorry, I made it a bad thing. I'm young in international cricket, and I'm sorry. Which he obviously did. But I think he would have gotten a 50 per cent match fee from the ICC. Steve Smith would have played the next Test match. David Warner, they would have played the whole rest of the year. But what ended up happening is they missed a year of cricket,” he added.For du Plessis, the Sandpaper Gate scandal was therefore not only about what happened on the field, but also about how the aftermath was handled. He believes the punishment, political pressure and public reaction turned an already serious incident into a much bigger crisis for Smith, Warner and Bancroft.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Umpires' calls and different ball': Joe Root explains lean run as he chases Sachin Tendulkar’s record
articles.summary: Cricket News: Joe Root has played down concerns over his indifferent batting form this English summer, insisting his experience and record give him confidence that .
articles.body: Joe Root has played down concerns over his indifferent batting form this English summer, insisting his experience and record give him confidence that he will find a way through the difficult patch as he continues his pursuit of Sachin Tendulkar’s record Test run tally.Root, who is chasing Tendulkar’s record of 15,921 Test runs, has crossed 50 only twice this home summer and is averaging 29.44. It is his second-lowest home season average since making his international debut 14 years ago.The 35-year-old has also been dismissed LBW nine times in his last seven Tests, including seven times this summer. Root, however, believes the conditions have made batting unusually difficult across the board.Root points to testing conditions“I've played this game a long time and I've always found ways of solving those problems and working it through,” Root told the BBC after the Lord's Test against Pakistan.“I don't see this as being any different. There's a reason why I've got 14,000 runs (14,208) and a reason why I've played the best part of 15 years at this level.“Of course it's frustrating that there's sort of a trend. There are probably four umpires' calls within that, which could have gone the other way, and the ball is probably deviating more than it ever has.”Root also pointed towards the Dukes ball as one possible reason for the unusually testing conditions faced by batters this summer. He suggested there had been a noticeable difference from last season, when England and India pushed for ball changes multiple times during their series.“The balls have been different this summer,” he said. “I think there is a different lacquer. They were worried about it going out of shape. They are denting surfaces more.”Despite his lean run, Root remains confident that he can find a solution.“You try and be realistic and understand where everything's at, but also be aware of what you need to do to keep improving and keep getting better. I'm pretty sure I'll get through the other side. I'm not too concerned about that.”‘You’re never given anything in this game’Root’s pursuit of Tendulkar’s record has brought his run-scoring under greater scrutiny, but the England batter used his current struggles to underline just how difficult sustained success in Test cricket can be.“You're never given anything in this game,” said Root. “You have to work for everything. You have to keep working hard and I'll certainly keep doing that.“You're constantly going to get challenged and you're constantly going to have to look to evolve and learn, but that's never been something I've shied away from and I certainly won't be doing moving forward.”Root’s batting struggles have not prevented England from making a strong start to his second stint as captain. England beat Pakistan by 194 runs at Lord’s to seal the series, giving Root two wins from two Tests since returning to the leadership role and England their first Test series win since 2024.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Everyone is worried’: Pakistan languish at WTC bottom after another heavy defeat
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan’s Test crisis deepened at Lord’s as another heavy away defeat left them languishing at the bottom of the World Test Championship standings, w.
articles.body: Pakistan’s Test crisis deepened at Lord’s as another heavy away defeat left them languishing at the bottom of the World Test Championship standings, with pacer Mohammad Abbas admitting that “everyone is worried” about the team’s performances.Pakistan’s fortunes in the longest format have declined significantly in recent years, both at home and overseas.Their latest setback was a 194-run defeat to England at Lord’s, following an innings defeat in the series opener at Leeds. It was Pakistan’s 10th loss in their last 11 away Tests.‘Our performance is a concern for everyone’Abbas, who finished the Lord’s Test with nine wickets and claimed his first five-wicket haul at the venue, acknowledged that Pakistan are fully aware of the problems facing them.“Our performance is a concern for everyone. Everyone is worried, including selection committee and the NCA. We're not doing well, we accept that. We're not batting, bowling or fielding well and we discuss this all the time in meetings. We're all working on it, and we need to be, too,” Abbas said after the Lord’s defeat.The pacer singled out Pakistan’s fielding as one area that needs considerable improvement. Dropped catches proved costly as England’s key batters were allowed to add significantly to their total.“We dropped catches, and their key players scored 70-odd extra runs. That's where the match changed because we could have bowled them out for 200. It's disappointing,” Abbas said.Despite his own impressive showing, the veteran pacer remained frustrated that his individual performances have not translated into victories.“Individual performances are important, but I try to perform to help the team win. It's been many matches that I've been performing, but the team hasn't won,” he said.‘Experience is very important in Test cricket’Abbas also pointed to the relative inexperience of Pakistan’s current pace attack as another challenge.“In Bangladesh, we had a different bowling combination to here. We won a Test in the West Indies. The guys are adjusting, but experience is very important in Test cricket,” he said.Abbas, who has played 32 Tests, said the younger fast bowlers alongside him are still adapting to the demands of international cricket across different conditions.“I've played 32 Test matches, but the fast bowlers playing with me are very new to Test cricket. But everybody is trying to improve.”Pakistan now have one more opportunity to avoid a series whitewash and collect valuable WTC points when they face England in the third Test at Edgbaston, beginning September 9.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
